sections.heading: Overview
bullets: Priya Raman led a 15-minute weekly product sync on customer requests, sales pipeline feedback, support trends, and evidence needed for the next planning cycle.

sections.heading: Key points
bullets: Amara Nwosu found 27 product-related support requests in two weeks, including 11 import or report-speed tickets from six carriers; seven concerned bulk import and four concerned reports.

Amara said Harbor Logistics values the live map and auto-assign, but its bulk import gives unhelpful errors when some rows fail, and Rafael estimated around 40 minutes searching for bad cells on a difficult Monday.
Daniel Ortiz said Acme Freight operates 140 trucks, has roughly $60,000 in approved annual budget, needs a security review, and expects to decide by the end of the next month.
Lucas Ferreira said aggregate ETA accuracy is about 82 percent, while some lanes and pickup windows perform worse and require analysis before any improvement is promised.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Priya, Daniel, Amara, and Lucas agreed to gather customer files, prospect examples, support counts, and lane-level ETA data before deciding product scope.
Priya said driver mobile app v2, ETA accuracy, and self-serve onboarding are candidates for the upcoming Q4 planning discussion, not approved bets.
Priya will prepare a one-page evidence sheet by Friday that separates existing customer impact, prospective revenue, sample sizes, timing, and unresolved questions.

sections.heading: Open questions
bullets: Lucas still needs to determine whether the slow reports share one expensive query and whether the three redacted import files reveal one common validation failure.
The group has not established whether prospects need a reusable migration feature, an assisted setup, or a narrower import reliability fix.
Amara will research whether requests for automated exports represent an API need before any API work is prioritized.

sections.heading: Pain points
bullets: Daniel said Acme Freight's spreadsheet-and-phone dispatch process leaves customers without live arrival times and makes idle drivers hard to identify.
Amara said Harbor Logistics loses an estimated 40 minutes on a difficult Monday when bulk import fails without identifying the problematic rows.

sections.heading: Current solution
bullets: Daniel said Acme Freight currently coordinates much of its 140-truck operation with spreadsheets and phone calls.
Amara said Harbor Logistics already uses Kestrel Dispatch's live map and auto-assign and uploads route sheets with several hundred stops.

sections.heading: Budget and timeline
bullets: Daniel said Acme Freight has approximately $60,000 in approved annual budget, requires a security review, and expects to choose a vendor by the end of next month.

sections.heading: Objections
bullets: Daniel said Acme's Tom worries that cleaning years of records for migration will take too much of his dispatch team's time.
Lucas warned that the team does not yet know Acme's data schemas and cannot promise migration of historical records or an ETA improvement.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Daniel will bring three more prospect migration examples by Friday and arrange an Acme discussion about file shapes and security this week.
Amara will compare prospect needs with existing customer import failures, while Priya will keep unapproved product features out of the sales promise.

sections.heading: Yesterday
bullets: Daniel Ortiz held the Acme Freight discovery call yesterday and heard that migration effort, live ETAs, and security review matter to its buying decision.

sections.heading: Today
bullets: Amara Nwosu will attach three redacted import examples to the issue today and identify what each customer expected versus what Dispatch accepted.
Priya Raman will collect the mobile app, import, and ETA evidence for a one-page planning input due Friday.
Lucas Ferreira will examine the import files tomorrow and prepare slow report and lane-level ETA samples by Friday.

sections.heading: Blockers
bullets: Lucas Ferreira cannot size a row-level import error fix until he has examined the three redacted customer files.
Daniel Ortiz cannot responsibly promise Acme a general migration feature because its data schemas and reusable demand are still unknown.
Amara Nwosu has five ETA accuracy complaints to deduplicate before treating them as five distinct customer reports.

sections.heading: Goals
bullets: Priya Raman wanted the group to identify the strongest customer problems and gather evidence for the next planning cycle without settling the Q4 roadmap.

sections.heading: Progress
bullets: Amara Nwosu separated 11 import and report-speed tickets from six carriers into seven bulk-import tickets and four slow-report tickets.
Daniel Ortiz brought feedback from Acme Freight's 140-truck operation and its roughly $60,000 annual budget.

sections.heading: Risks
bullets: Priya said one promising sales deal should not by itself determine a reusable migration feature, while Daniel warned that Acme has a real decision window.
Lucas said the 82 percent ETA accuracy figure masks weak lanes and may make a product proposal look more certain than the data supports.
Amara warned that self-serve onboarding could shift import failures onto new customers if row-level errors remain unclear.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: The group agreed to investigate a narrow import fix and an assisted Acme setup before committing to broader product work.
Priya said mobile v2, ETA accuracy, and self-serve onboarding remain options for the later Q4 planning meeting.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Amara will provide redacted import examples today and deduplicated support counts and Harbor notes tomorrow.
Lucas will review the import files tomorrow and share slow-report jobs and four weeks of lane-level ETA analysis by Friday.
Daniel will collect three prospect migration examples, while Priya will circulate the planning evidence sheet by Friday.
